title: [replay] fix(desktop): turning the camera off and on mid-take keeps the face in its own track
body:
> **Replay of [niway-dev/kaipu-record#463](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/463)** for the code-review benchmark. Base `c58b68f`, head `3ec7a13`: the same commits the original reviewers saw, so the diff is byte-identical. Never merged. Method and scoring: [wachiman/docs/benchmark](https://github.com/niway-dev/wachiman/tree/main/docs/benchmark). The original description follows.

---

## What this does

During a take that records a webcam file, turning the camera off and on again now keeps the face in its own track:

- **Off:** the camera bubble window is hidden and kept (parked), still content-protected. Both camera streams stop, so the camera light goes off: the bubble's own preview and the recorder's webcam capture. The webcam file keeps running on the same clock and repeats its last frame.
- **On:** the same native window is shown again. The recorder opens the camera again and writes into the **same** `<name>.webcam.mp4`, with the same encoder settings.
- **Gaps:** each off period is saved in the sidecar as `webcam.gaps: [{ startMs, endMs }]`, in screen ms. The editor seeds each gap as a hidden webcam segment, so the lane shows it striped and export and Share leave the face out there. If the camera is still off when the take stops, that last period is a trailing gap that ends with the take.
- **Re-open fails** (camera denied, busy or unplugged): the fallback is the same as today. The webcam file ends at that point, the bubble is unprotected so the face goes into the screen, and the existing "camera wasn't available" notice appears after the take.
- **Unchanged:** outside a take, after it, and during the countdown, turning the camera off still destroys the window, which releases the device. A take that started with the camera off keeps the legacy path: a bubble turned on mid-take is burned into the screen.

No Linear ticket: the workspace has hit its issue limit.

## Why

Owner QA on real takes. The camera was on at the start, turned off at about 8 s, then turned on again. The webcam file stopped at 8 s (the lane was half full), and after the camera came back the bubble was burned into the screen recording.

The cause: the old code destroyed the window on camera off. A bubble window created mid-take, unprotected, is captured by the running stream. The webcam file also could not continue, because mediabunny's `MediaStreamVideoTrackSource` is bound to a single track.

## What to review

- `apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-hub.ts:304-336`: park vs destroy (`takeRecordsWebcam`), the replacement window when the webcam file ended while parked, and `releaseParkedBubble` at finalize, abort, stop and forced reset.
- `apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/camera-bubble-window.ts:236,262`: `placedBounds` (a trailing gap still records where the bubble was) and `park`. `ready-to-show` respects a park.
- `apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/bubble-protection.ts`: `recordsWebcam()`.
- `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/camera-bubble/camera-bubble.tsx:44`: the preview follows the Camera toggle.
- `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/webcam-relay.ts:48`: the relay track (`MediaStreamTrackGenerator` fed through `MediaStreamTrackProcessor`).
- `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:658-709`: the encoder reads the relay, with `frameRate` and `sizeChangeBehavior`. `:769-800`: `turnWebcamOff` / `turnWebcamOn`, including supersession and the re-open timeout.
- `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts:806,928,1017`: gap times on the take's clock, the forwarder, and the gaps sent with finalize.
- `apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/webcam-track.ts:131`: `sanitizeWebcamGaps`.
- `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/webcam/webcam-model.ts:135`: gap seeding.

## Decisions

- **A relay track instead of a hand-driven `VideoSampleSource`.** mediabunny keeps doing what it already does: the synced-zero t0 that the start offset is read from, the pause offset, constant-frame-rate pacing and dropping frames under backpressure. So the existing offset and pause rules hold without being re-implemented.
- **Explicit `frameRate`, taken from the camera's own settings** (30 if it reports none). That is the rate mediabunny used to read from the camera track itself, so the encoding is the same. It is also what makes the file keep running through a gap: mediabunny repeats the last frame on the clock.
- **`sizeChangeBehavior: "contain"`, only with the relay.** It does nothing unless a camera opened again delivers a different size (for example after a fallback). Without it, the default `deny` would make that whole webcam file unusable. Codec, bitrate, hardware acceleration and latency mode are unchanged.
- **A gap closes when the first new frame reaches the file**, not when the toggle flips. Otherwise the held frame would show while the camera warms up.
- **Gaps shorter than 1 s are stretched to the minimum segment length.** The session parser drops shorter segments on reload. The stretched segment stays inside the recording when its length is known.
- **No relay** (no `MediaStreamTrackGenerator`), **or a toggle during the countdown:** the previous rule applies (off ends the file).
- **The editor fingerprint is not changed.** It already hashes `scene.webcam`, so seeded segments are covered automatically. The export fill-frame logic is not changed either: the held frames in a gap are drawn through `webcamAt`, which hides them. Finalize and webcam-ended handling are not changed: a gap is not an end.

## Unverified assumptions

- **Owner check needed:** that ScreenCaptureKit keeps a hidden-then-shown window (same native window id) excluded from the stream that is already running. This PR depends on it, and I could not run the app here.
- That `MediaStreamTrackGenerator` and `MediaStreamTrackProcessor` exist in Electron 39's renderer (Chromium ships both on `window`). If they are missing, the take silently uses the previous rule.
- That a `VideoFrame` from a camera that has been stopped stays valid, so it can be repeated through the gap.
- On re-open failure: that a running stream picks up a bubble that drops its protection. This is the same best-effort mechanism as today's unplug path.

## Checks

- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run` (apps/kaipu-record): 328 files, 3387 tests passed. The new tests cover the hub and bubble window with fakes, the bubble's toggle, the relay, the engine relay path, the store gaps, sanitize, and seeding.
- `bun run check-types`: passes.
- oxlint: 0 warnings in the touched files. `oxfmt --check`: passes. Pre-push `verify-local`: passed.
- Not run: Electron, the app, or E2E.

## How to test it yourself

1. `bun run dev`, open Record, turn the camera on, and record the whole display.
2. At about 5 s, turn the camera off from the control bar. **Expect:** the bubble disappears and the camera light turns off.
3. At about 10 s, turn the camera on again. **Expect:** the bubble comes back in the same place and the light turns on.
4. Stop at about 15 s and open the take in the editor. **Expect:** the webcam lane has faces before and after a striped hidden segment from about 5 s to 10 s, and playback hides the face there.
5. Open the raw screen file (`<id>.mp4` in the vault): **no bubble at any time**. Open `<id>.webcam.mp4`: it runs the whole take, with a frozen frame during the gap.
6. Do a take that ends with the camera off (turn it off at about 5 s, stop at about 10 s). **Expect:** a striped segment from about 5 s to the end, the light off from 5 s, and the bubble window gone after the take.
7. Camera-busy re-open case: start a take with the camera on, turn it off, open the camera in another app that holds it exclusively (or unplug an external camera), then turn the camera on in Kaipu. **Expect:** within about 3 s the bubble falls back into the screen recording, the webcam lane ends at the gap, and after the take the notice "The camera wasn't available, so your face was recorded in the screen instead." appears.
8. Regression check: start a take with the camera **off** and turn it on mid-take. **Expect:** the bubble is burned into the screen recording, as before (legacy path).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * You can now turn the camera off and back on during a recording while keeping the webcam video track intact when supported.
  * Camera-off periods are recorded as gaps and appear as hidden segments in the video editor.
  * The camera preview now reflects camera settings, including settings updated during use.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * The camera bubble can be hidden and restored during webcam recording without losing its position or protection. It is cleaned up when recording ends or the webcam track is no longer active.
